subject: Post-demo follow-up: privacy items & evidence requests
messages:
From: Tom Brenner <tbrenner@avahealth.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.example.com>
Cc: Sara Hendrix <sarah@avahealth.com>, Ava Health Legal <legal@avahealth.com>
Date: 2026-10-03T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo follow-up — DPA clarifications and evidence

Thanks again for the demo this morning — the team liked the latency numbers. A few follow-ups from our security/privacy review: 

1) Role mapping: can you confirm whether Redwood will be the processor or a subprocessor for inference calls that include patient PII?
2) Subprocessors: we need a current list and whether any subprocessor has access to raw request payloads.
3) Breach notice: what is your standard notification window and What will you commit to in the DPA?
4) Logging & retention: we need to understand default log retention (request/response logs, audit trails) and options to shorten retention for PHI.
5) Data residency: can the inference workload be pinned to us-east-1 and guarantee no cross-region replication for payloads?

Can you send a concise memo and any artifacts (SOC2, certs, DPA redline) we can share with Legal? Prefer to have this in the next 72 hours if possible — our procurement timeline is tight.

-Tom
Tom Brenner
Director of IT Security
Ava Health
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.example.com>
To: Tom Brenner <tbrenner@avahealth.com>
Cc: Sara Hendrix <sarah@avahealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com>
Date: 2026-10-03T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo follow-up — DPA clarifications and evidence

Tom — great to meet you this morning. High-level answers up front, then attachments and next steps below.

Quick answers:
- Role: Redwood will be a processor for inference and embeddings requests outlined in the SOW. We can include language in the DPA that reflects processor obligations and limits of processing.
- Subprocessors: attached is the current subprocessor list (redwood-subprocessor-list-20261003.csv). Most infra providers are limited to managing the runtime and do not get access to raw payloads on hosted Dedicated deployments; we’ll flag any that could see payloads.
- Breach notice: our standard practice is to provide an initial acknowledgement within 48 hours of detection and a follow-up with remediation details within 30 days; we can discuss tighter windows if needed for PHI.
- Logging & retention: default request/response logs are retained 90 days. For PHI workloads we offer scoped retention (30/14/0 days) under contract and can disable request body retention while retaining minimal audit metadata.
- Residency: we support region pinning (us-east-1). For Private/Dedicated customers we can ensure inference stays within the requested region and document the lack of cross-region replication for payloads.

Attachments: 
- redwood-dpa-redline-v1.pdf (initial DPA with our suggested redlines)
- redwood-subprocessor-list-20261003.csv (current subs)
- dataflow-avah-poc.png (high-level dataflow for the demo)

Next steps I suggest: 
1) Karthik (legal) to review and provide concrete alternate DPA language if anything is non-starter.
2) Tom/Sara — confirm whether you need retention set to 30/14/0 days or body-scrubbing.
3) We can run a short technical runbook review with your infra/security team next week to validate residency and logging controls.

Looping in Karthik and Marissa for legal/accounting items. Happy to hop on a 30-min call to walk Legal through the attachments.

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com>
To: Ava Health Legal <legal@avahealth.com>, Tom Brenner <tbrenner@avahealth.com>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.example.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example.com>
Date: 2026-10-05T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo follow-up — DPA clarifications and evidence

Hi Tom / Ava Legal — I reviewed the DPA redline Tessa attached and here are our clarifications and proposed compromise language for the main items you raised. Please treat this as a starting point for redline exchange.

1) Controller/Processor: Redwood will operate as a Processor for the inference service; the customer (Ava Health) is the Controller for any patient data processed via calls to the service. We will add explicit language confirming: (a) processing only on documented instructions; (b) no use of customer data for model training; (c) adherence to documented deletion and retention policies.

2) Subprocessors: the attached CSV enumerates subprocessors and role access. For Hosted and Dedicated we segregate KV/cache and persistent storage; only a small set of infra providers have access to encrypted disk snapshots for capacity ops. We commit to customer notification of new subprocessors 30 days before onboarding, with an expedited notification and right to object for high-risk subs.

3) Breach notification: we propose the following contract language: initial acknowledgement within 48 hours of detection; interim update within 7 days with scope of impact; final report within 30 days. For confirmed exfiltration of PHI we will commit to a prioritized investigation and escalation path. If Ava requires a shorter contractual SLA for initial notice (e.g., 24 hours), we can discuss but that will require an elevated support level.

4) Logging & retention: default = 90 days; options = 30 / 14 / 0 days for request bodies. Audit metadata (timestamp, request size, model id, customer id) can be retained longer for billing/troubleshooting but we can redact PII from logs by default. We will provide an export of retention settings and a short runbook for toggling retention for pilots.

5) Residency: we can pin inference to us-east-1 for hosted customers and guarantee no cross-region payload replication; for Dedicated and Private we can provide VPC-level controls. We will include a residency addendum in the DPA.

Attachments: I am attaching a suggested DPA paragraph for breach timelines and a short FAQ we use with other medtech customers (attached as redwood-dpa-redline-v1.pdf).

If this looks broadly acceptable, Marissa will coordinate the commercial SOW and we can set a date for the technical deep dive.

-Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference
From: Sara Hendrix <sarah@avahealth.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.example.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com>
Cc: Tom Brenner <tbrenner@avahealth.com>, Ava Health Legal <legal@avahealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example.com>
Date: 2026-10-06T15:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo follow-up — DPA clarifications and evidence

Thanks — that's helpful and gives Legal a lot to work with. A few clarifying notes from our side after an initial review: 

- Can you confirm ‘‘no use for training’’ is included as a non-negotiable clause (we need explicit prohibition)?
- Please provide a redacted example of the request/response log format (just metadata + example body scrubbing) so our InfoSec can validate scrubbing capabilities.
- For subprocessors we will review the CSV and flag any providers that need additional info; can you confirm your standard 30-day notification and the escalation path for objections?
- Residency: confirm that for the POC we can enable us-east-1 pinning and that telemetry/metrics aggregates but not raw payloads may be processed outside region for platform ops (we will accept aggregated telemetry).

Next steps from Ava: we will get our redline back to you by EOD Friday (2026-10-08) and would like to schedule the technical runbook review for week of 10/12. Marissa — if you can send SOW guidelines and an estimated cost for a 3-week pilot (dedicated small pool, retention set to 30 days) that would be great.

Attachment requests: sample log export (CSV stub), SOC2 Type II report URL or cert, confirmation of encryption at rest key management approach.

Best,
Sara Hendrix
Compliance & Risk
Ava Health
